analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/developer/test.md, head lines 551-561. It adds a `swift test --skip-build --filter 'LocalTokenizerByteFallbackTests'` command and a description of that suite. The suite loads a synthetic tokenizer with Gemma 4's decoder sequence through the production LocalTokenizerLoader. It checks that `<0xHH>` byte-fallback tokens survive a whole decode, a stream, a segment restart and a trailing special token. It also checks that a run cut inside a character ends in one U+FFFD, that the unknown token does not read as a byte, and that a literal `<0x41>` token on another decoder keeps its spelling. I traced the change against the threat model. It adds no runtime code, no credentials, no network access, no endpoints and no change to trust boundaries or key handling. The text says tests use synthetic tokenizers and no model weights, and it asks for no secrets or production state. The new text does not touch coordinator-to-provider encryption (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), the installer path (TB-013) or the prefix cache (T-041). The rest of the file is unchanged context. It carries guidance such as isolated state, never using production cache roots or keys, and exclusive GPU lanes, and none of that is weakened. The only security-adjacent point is that tokenizer decode correctness affects output integrity, not confidentiality. The added test documentation improves regression coverage and creates no new attack surface. The documented test file `LocalTokenizerByteFallbackTests` is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm it exists or does what the text says. That is a coverage limit, not a finding, and no security conclusion depends on it.
